title: Measure distillation interaction and select an RGA pairing
physicalPurpose: Separate a binary feed into qualified overhead and bottoms products while recognizing that reflux and reboiler steam affect both compositions.
principalTechnique: Open-loop interaction testing and Relative Gain Array pairing
objective: Measure all four local input-output gains, calculate the Relative Gain Array, and select a defensible decentralized pairing before designing controllers.

simplifications: The model describes local composition deviations around one qualified operating point rather than absolute product compositions.
Four stable first-order path states retain unequal 20, 35, 40 and 30 second response times and all four steady input-output gains.
Tray hydraulics, analyzer delay, flooding, weeping, inventories and the physical safety system are outside this simulation.
Configured coefficients generate the plant but do not replace gain estimates calculated from the two executed step records.
Simulation-only I/O and evidence; no physical column, reflux valve or reboiler-steam valve is operated.

baseline.limitation: Tag names and isolated direct gains do not show how closing the second loop changes the effective gain and feedback direction.

change.decision: Accept the diagonal overhead-to-reflux and bottoms-to-reboiler pairing only from four valid measured gains and reject the negative-relative-gain cross pairing.

disturbances: Run a restored 20-second zero-input baseline followed by a 180-second +5-percentage-point reflux step while reboiler steam remains zero.
Start a new restored run and apply the equivalent reboiler-steam step while reflux remains zero.
Estimate all four gains from final-window means and calculate the determinant and Relative Gain Array from those measured values.

acceptance.window: last 10 seconds of the independently restored reflux-step record
last 10 seconds of the independently restored reflux-step record
last 10 seconds of the independently restored reboiler-step record
last 10 seconds of the independently restored reboiler-step record
calculation from the four qualified measured steady-state gains
63.2-percent crossing relative to the finite-record settled-change estimate for all four paths

abortPredicates: Any required input or composition signal is nonfinite, stale, forced or invalid.
Either input leaves -10 through +10 percentage points or either composition deviation leaves -6 through +6 percentage points.
The non-excited input moves more than 0.02 percentage points during an identification record.
Authority, plant identity, sample schedule or restoration state differs between records.
The absolute applied step is below 4.95 percentage points or an output does not meet the settling rule.
safety.restorationMode: Keep Manual authority, return both simulated input changes to zero, verify both applied inputs and composition deviations restore, then begin a new record.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer with the responsible distillation operations and process-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical distillation column, reflux valve or reboiler-steam valve is operated.
The local Simulation matrix does not qualify another operating point or physical column.
Physical testing requires reviewed topology, process and safety limits, perturbation and dwell, product disposition, abort and restoration procedures, and explicit immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Execute two safe interaction tests, construct a measured gain matrix, calculate the Relative Gain Array, and justify a distillation pairing.
requiredVisibleEvidence: requested and applied reflux and reboiler changes

learning.context: A continuous binary distillation column uses reflux and reboiler steam to regulate overhead and bottoms product quality near one operating point.
learning.reason: Lesson 60 localized a final-element fault; with healthy valves here, genuine two-input, two-output process interaction must be measured before pairing loops.
theory: Each steady-state gain is one settled output change divided by one independently applied input change.
The gain matrix records all four signed local paths.
The Relative Gain Array compares open-loop and closed-loop effective gains and exposes negative or strongly interacting pairings.
Pairing evidence is local to the qualified operating point and does not design or stabilize controllers.
learning.workedPrediction: Separate +5-percentage-point steps predict output changes of [+4.00, -1.50] and [-2.00, +3.50], gain matrix [[0.8, -0.4], [-0.3, 0.7]], determinant 0.44 and RGA [[1.2727, -0.2727], [-0.2727, 1.2727]].
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, Manual authority, signal quality, timing, requested/applied inputs, outputs, limits and zero restoration.
Define input/output changes, steady-state gains, settling, determinant, RGA elements and pairing rules before results.
learning.baseline: Recognize that names and direct open-loop gains alone do not establish a safe decentralized pairing.
learning.change: Execute one restored step per input, estimate all four gains, and form the Relative Gain Array from measured records.
learning.comparison: Hold model, initial state, timing, step magnitude, limits, seed and windows equal while changing only the excited input.
learning.validation: Require settled independent records, four gains within tolerance, all four response times within the finite-record tolerance, nonsingular inversion, row/column sums near one and positive diagonal versus negative cross relative gains.
learning.explanation: Closing one loop changes the effective gain available to the other; the RGA selects the diagonal pairing but does not remove its remaining interaction.
learning.transfer: Repeat all four path measurements after material operating-point changes; Lesson 62 tests whether decentralized PI needs justified decoupling.
